title: Upper limb & axial anatomy · Past year 3

Full includes five axial/thoracic items; Upper only excludes them. Q19 has no correct offered choice and remains ungraded. Spelling is normalized and substantive stem repairs are disclosed.

questions.prompt: Identify the fracture-dislocation of the forearm shown.
questions.note: The retained image shows a proximal ulnar fracture with dislocation of the radial head: a Monteggia injury. The screenshot's stem is cropped to 'forearm?'; the neutral identification instruction is an explicit editorial reconstruction from the visible image and choices.

questions.prompt: Superior and inferior radioulnar joints are classified as:
questions.note: The proximal and distal radioulnar joints are synovial pivot joints. The intervening interosseous membrane is a syndesmosis, not one of these two joints.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the anatomical snuffbox?
options: Extensor pollicis longus forms its ulnar border.
The trapezoid is palpable at its base.
It is most obvious with the thumb fully abducted.
It contains the posterior interosseous artery.
questions.note: EPL forms the medial/ulnar border. The floor is scaphoid and trapezium, and the artery is radial. Extension tensions the bounding tendons; 'abducted' alone is imprecise compared with the unequivocal border in A.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Ulnar nerve injury causes paralysis of all of the following except:
options: Medial half of flexor digitorum profundus
questions.note: Abductor pollicis brevis is normally median supplied. The other muscles are ulnar supplied; whether forearm muscles are affected depends on how proximal the injury is.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve branches from a trunk of the brachial plexus?
questions.note: The nerve to subclavius arises from the superior trunk. Dorsal scapular and long thoracic arise from roots; subscapular nerves arise from the posterior cord.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement about the musculocutaneous nerve is correct?
options: It arises from the lateral cord of the brachial plexus.
It terminates as the posterior interosseous nerve.
questions.note: It arises from the lateral cord and continues as the lateral cutaneous nerve of forearm. Brachioradialis is radial supplied; brachialis commonly has a lateral radial contribution, making 'all' misleading.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: What is the nerve supply of palmaris brevis?
options: Palmar branch of the median nerve
Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
Recurrent branch of the median nerve
questions.note: Palmaris brevis receives a motor branch from the superficial ulnar division, unlike most ulnar intrinsic muscles supplied by the deep branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Through which opening does a hiatal hernia occur?
questions.note: A hiatal hernia involves the esophageal hiatus. Morgagni and Bochdalek defects are other diaphragmatic hernia sites.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: /study/reviews/cvs.pdf#page=23 — CVS review: Diaphragm and hernias. This is an axial item, outside the limb review outline.

questions.prompt: Which nerve usually accompanies the superior ulnar collateral artery?
questions.note: The superior ulnar collateral artery accompanies the ulnar nerve through the medial intermuscular septum toward the posterior aspect of the medial epicondyle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve passes through the quadrangular space?
questions.note: The axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral vessels pass through the quadrangular space. The radial nerve passes through the triangular interval.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The palmar metacarpal and radialis indicis arteries originate from which arteries, respectively?
options: Superficial palmar arch; first dorsal metacarpal artery
First dorsal metacarpal artery; radial artery
questions.note: Palmar metacarpal arteries arise from the deep arch. Radialis indicis normally arises from the radial system, often in association with princeps pollicis; variants exist.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement about the median nerve is correct?
options: It supplies all of flexor digitorum profundus.
questions.note: B is unequivocally correct. The normal nerve passes between pronator teres heads, deep to its humeral head; 'under pronator teres' is vague but defensible, and anatomical variants pass deep to both heads. B and C are accepted rather than penalizing that wording. The medial half of FDP is usually ulnar supplied.
questions.subject: anatomy
evidence: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5380802/ — cadaveric relationships of median nerve and pronator teres heads.

questions.prompt: Which is not a named branch of the axillary artery?
questions.note: The standard axillary branches include superior thoracic, thoracoacromial, lateral thoracic, subscapular and the two circumflex humeral arteries. 'Medial thoracic' is not a standard named axillary branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which muscle classically initiates shoulder abduction?
options: Anterior and posterior fibers of deltoid
questions.note: Supraspinatus is the traditional answer for initiating the first part of abduction. It cooperates with deltoid rather than switching off when deltoid becomes the dominant elevator.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which structure is located inside the vertebral canal in the cervical region?
questions.note: The posterior longitudinal ligament lies inside the vertebral canal. Its superior continuation, the tectorial membrane, is also internal; the apical ligament of the dens lies in the craniovertebral canal anterior to the tectorial membrane. A, B and D are accepted for this broad wording. The anterior longitudinal ligament is outside, anterior to the bodies.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The rotator cuff is formed by all of the following except:
questions.note: The cuff is supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor and subscapularis. Teres major is not a cuff muscle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement about the lumbricals is correct?
options: They oppose the action of interossei.
They arise from flexor digitorum superficialis.
They aid flexion of the terminal phalanx.
They are all supplied by the ulnar nerve.
questions.note: No offered statement is correct as written. Lumbricals arise from FDP tendons, assist MCP flexion and IP extension with the interossei, and the first two are usually median supplied. The source is retained ungraded; no distractor is silently rewritten into a correct answer.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not normally pierce the clavipectoral fascia?
questions.note: The lateral pectoral nerve, thoracoacromial vessels, cephalic vein and lymphatics pierce the costocoracoid part. The medial pectoral nerve characteristically pierces pectoralis minor rather than being one of these named contents.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: The flexor retinaculum attaches to all of the following except:
questions.note: Its attachments include the hook of hamate, pisiform, scaphoid tubercle and trapezium. Capitate is not a main retinacular attachment.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve is a branch of the posterior cord of the brachial plexus?
questions.note: Thoracodorsal arises from the posterior cord. Musculocutaneous arises from the lateral cord; long thoracic and dorsal scapular arise from roots.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve supplies the skin at the tip of the index finger?
questions.note: The median digital nerves supply the pulp and distal dorsal/nail-bed region of the index finger. Superficial radial supply is more proximal on its dorsal surface.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which statement about biceps brachii is correct?
options: Its short head arises from the acromion.
It is supplied by the median nerve.
Its long head arises from the greater tubercle.
questions.note: Biceps is a strong forearm supinator, especially with the elbow flexed. Its short head arises from coracoid, long head from supraglenoid/labral attachments, and motor supply is musculocutaneous.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which artery anastomoses with the middle collateral artery?
questions.note: The middle collateral branch of profunda brachii participates in the posterior lateral elbow network with the interosseous recurrent artery. The radial collateral usually meets radial recurrent anteriorly.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Through which listed muscle does the deep radial/posterior interosseous nerve pass?
questions.note: The deep branch of radial nerve traverses supinator and continues as the posterior interosseous nerve. The source's 'can pass through all of following muscles' is an apparent wording error; it does not pass through all four.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which vertebral region has a short spinous process, triangular vertebral canal and kidney-shaped body?
questions.note: The large kidney-shaped body and short broad spinous process characterize lumbar vertebrae; their vertebral foramen is triangular.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: What is the motor nerve of the diaphragm and how does it reach the diaphragm?
options: Phrenic nerve through the aortic opening at T12
Vagus nerve through the esophageal opening at T10
Phrenic nerve through the caval opening at T8
Vagus nerve through the caval opening at T10
questions.note: Phrenic nerves provide motor supply. C is the intended answer for the right phrenic nerve or its terminal branches accompanying the IVC at the caval opening near T8. The left phrenic nerve pierces the diaphragm separately; the route must not be generalized to both sides.
